Where to Stay in Ranong?
12 Stays We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Twelve Ranong stays across every budget — an in-town hotel piping hot mineral water into your room, a mangrove-villa resort on Koh Phayam, and an old-town hostel from ฿250. Covering the spots travellers actually use: the town, the Raksawarin hot-spring area, Pak Nam and Koh Phayam island. Starting from around ฿250–3,200/night.
introH2: ♨️ Why does choosing the right base in Ranong matter so much?
introHtml: Ranong is the hot-spring town that many people only drive through or overnight in before catching the boat to Koh Phayam and Koh Chang — but it has natural hot springs, quiet beaches and islands that feel genuinely different, so matching your stay to what you want to do matters more than the hotel itself. Ranong town is the hub for food, markets and the Sino-Portuguese old quarter, ideal for walking around and connecting onward by road or boat · The Raksawarin hot-spring area (Bang Rin) is the side within walking distance of the hot springs, ideal if you've come to soak · Pak Nam Ranong is the seafront near the pier with views of the Myanmar-side islands · and Koh Phayam is a quiet island you reach by boat, ideal for sleeping right by the sea. Many travellers book without checking whether their stay is in town or out on the island, then lose time travelling back and forth every time they want to reach the centre or the sea. This guide brings together 12 Ranong stays we've reviewed across every tier — every pick comes from reading real guest reviews, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Ranong has no metro — the main ways to get around are by road, motorbike and boat. The town centre is walkable for the old quarter and markets, while the hot springs, Pak Nam and the pier are out of town, so driving or hailing a ride is easiest. Koh Phayam is a 45-minute to 2-hour boat ride from the Ranong pier, then motorbike on the island. The main areas in this guide: Town — Tinidee, A Day Inn, Greenish, TOBEDzZ, Ranong Backpacker's (old quarter, onward transport) · Raksawarin hot-spring area — THANSILA, Rattana's (walk to the hot springs) · Ngao area — Baroque Boutique (near the airport) · Pak Nam — Jansom Beach, B.C. Badin (seafront, Myanmar-side island views) · Koh Phayam — The Blue Sky, Lamai Koh Phayam (sleep by the sea).

entries.name: Tinidee Hotel@Ranong
entries.badge: ♨️ Hot mineral water in your room
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ranong town · Khao Niwet · walk to the market · 3.5 km to the hot spring
tags: ♨️ Hot mineral water piped into your bathroom
🏙️ In town, walk to the market
🚐 Free shuttle to the hot spring
entries.addr: 41/144 Tha Mueang Rd, Khao Niwet, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: Tinidee@Ranong is a town hotel that brings Ranong's signature into the room — natural hot mineral water piped into your bathroom, so you can soak in a mineral bath in your own room. It's a 7-storey, 133-room hotel, the most reviewed stay in this guide at 481 and ranked #3 of 17 Ranong hotels on TripAdvisor. Real reviews praise the spacious, clean, good-value rooms, the mineral pool, sauna and gym, and a location within walking distance of the town market. Worth knowing: it's an older, continuously maintained building, some nights carry noise from the hotel bar, and the walls in some rooms are not great for sound.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: After a day out, run the hot mineral bath in your own room — it's the thing guests mention most. If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a higher floor away from the bar zone. The hotel runs a free shuttle to soak at the Raksawarin hot spring — ask about times at check-in.
pros: Natural hot mineral water piped into your bathroom — a rare signature
In town, walk to the market and restaurants, 3.5 km to the hot spring
Spacious, clean, good-value rooms, with a mineral pool, sauna and gym
Friendly staff and a free shuttle to the Raksawarin hot spring
cons: Some nights carry noise from the hotel bar/pub · thin walls in some rooms
An older-style building and decor, not a brand-new boutique

entries.name: The Blue Sky Resort@ Koh Payam
entries.revCount: 19 reviews · round bungalows in the mangroves · open year-round
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Mae Mai beach · Koh Phayam · boat from Ranong pier
tags: 🌊 Water surrounds them at high tide
entries.addr: 44/3 Moo 1, Ao Mae Mai, Koh Phayam, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: The Blue Sky is a Koh Phayam resort built around round bungalows in the mangroves — at high tide the water surrounds them so they seem to float, a villa look that's hard to find elsewhere, scoring 8.2 and open year-round. Real reviews praise the romantic, quiet and private feel that suits couples and anyone escaping the crowds, the cleanliness, the clear water and a pool with a sea view. Worth knowing: the water only surrounds the bungalows at high tide (mudflats show at low tide), the Wi-Fi is slow across the whole island, and rooms and food cost more than other stays on the island — and you reach it by boat then motorbike.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the floating-on-water feel, check the tide times before booking. Book the Koh Phayam boat and your stay ahead, especially in high season. Bring your own essentials and cash, as shops on the island are limited.
pros: Round mangrove bungalows like nowhere else, water surrounds them at high tide
Quiet, private and romantic, good for couples
Good cleanliness, clear water, a pool with a sea view
Friendly staff and a nice beachfront restaurant
cons: Water only surrounds them at high tide · island-wide slow Wi-Fi · pricier than other island stays
Reached by boat and motorbike, needs planning ahead

entries.name: A Day Inn Ranong Hostel
entries.revCount: 263 reviews · highest score in this guide · Sino-Portuguese building
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town · Rueang Rat Rd · Ranong town
tags: 🎒 The highest score in this guide, 9.5
entries.addr: 204 Rueang Rat Rd, Khao Niwet, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: A Day Inn is the highest-scoring stay in this guide — 9.5 from 263 reviews, from just ฿250 a bed, in a Sino-Portuguese building in Ranong's old town. Real reviews agree on how clean both the rooms and shared bathrooms are, the friendly English-speaking owner and staff who book ferry tickets to Koh Phayam and arrange motorbike hire, the free local breakfast, and a location within walking distance of the market and restaurants. Its strengths are cleanliness, old-town charm and value. Worth knowing: it's a small hostel with limited private rooms, some rooms use shared bathrooms, and there's no pool or lift.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For privacy, pick a Standard Queen or Deluxe King with a private bathroom. Have the owner book your Koh Phayam ferry at check-in — easier than arranging it yourself. There aren't many rooms, so it fills fast in high season — book ahead.
pros: Very clean rooms and shared bathrooms — the highest score here, 9.5
Friendly, English-speaking owner and staff who help a great deal
Books Koh Phayam ferry tickets and arranges motorbike hire
Sino-Portuguese old-town building, walk to the market · free local breakfast
cons: Small hostel, limited private rooms · some rooms use shared bathrooms
No pool or lift · fills fast in high season

entries.name: Greenish Hotel
entries.revCount: 22 reviews · newly opened, clean and quiet
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Niwet · Ranong town · near the pier
tags: ✨ Newly opened, clean and quiet rooms
entries.addr: 98 Soi Ranong Phatthana 1, Khao Niwet, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: Greenish Hotel is a newly opened boutique hotel in town that stands out for cleanliness and quiet, scoring 8.6. Real reviews single out how new and clean the rooms feel, with spacious rooms, comfy beds and well-working bathrooms, friendly staff who help drop guests at restaurants, and a praised breakfast. It's within walking distance of a 7-Eleven, coffee shops and restaurants, and near the pier for the boat to Koh Phayam. Worth knowing: it's a small hotel with no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean stairs, there's no pool, and it's a little away from parts of the old quarter.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no lift, so if you'd rather avoid stairs, ask for a lower-floor room at booking. Staff can drop you at restaurants — ask at check-in. It's near the pier, handy as a base for the boat to Koh Phayam.
pros: Newly opened, very clean and quiet rooms — singled out in reviews
Spacious rooms, comfy beds, well-working bathrooms
Friendly staff who drop guests at restaurants · praised breakfast
Walk to a 7-Eleven and coffee shops, near the Koh Phayam pier · free parking
cons: Small hotel, no lift, upper floors mean stairs · no pool
A little away from parts of the old quarter · still few reviews

entries.name: TOBEDzZ Hotel
entries.revCount: 132 reviews · new, spacious rooms · by the bus station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Rin · Ranong town · by the bus station
tags: ✨ New, clean rooms, bigger than the price
🚌 By the bus station, 7-Eleven out front
entries.storyHtml: TOBEDzZ Hotel is a budget town hotel that stands out for new, clean rooms that are bigger than the price suggests, scoring 8.6 from 132 reviews. Real reviews single out the cleanliness and spaciousness of the rooms, comfy beds and good hot/cold water, a location right by the bus station that makes onward travel very easy, a 7-Eleven out front, and repeat guests who come back. Its strengths are value and the transport-friendly location. Worth knowing: as a budget hotel the facilities are limited with no pool, it's a fair way from the old quarter and the hot springs, and only some rooms have a bathtub.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a bathtub, pick a Deluxe King — only some rooms have one, so check the room type before booking. It's by the bus station, ideal for connecting onward. To reach the old quarter or hot springs, hailing a ride or having a car helps.
pros: New, very clean rooms, bigger than the price — singled out in reviews
Comfy beds, good hot and cold water
By the bus station, easy onward travel, 7-Eleven out front
Free parking, 24h front desk, luggage storage · good value
cons: Budget hotel, limited facilities, no pool
Away from the old quarter and hot springs · only some rooms have a bathtub

entries.name: Baroque Boutique Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ngao area · Mueang Ranong · near the airport
tags: 🌿 Shady garden with a fountain, quiet
entries.storyHtml: Baroque Boutique Resort is a tiny 6-room boutique in the Ngao area decorated with antiques, characterful in every corner, scoring 9.1. Real reviews praise the spotlessly clean, well-kept rooms, the unique decor and collectibles, an attentive owner who helps arrange trips and recommends places, a fresh-cooked breakfast to order, and a shady garden with a fountain that's quiet and private. Its strengths are the decor and a homely feel. Worth knowing: it's in the Ngao area, far from the town centre, the market and the pier, so a car is needed, with only 6 rooms it must be booked ahead, and the restaurant closes around 7 pm.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 6 rooms, book early. It's near Ranong airport, handy if you're flying in/out or have a car. The restaurant closes early, so if you arrive late, bring food or eat beforehand.
pros: Spotlessly clean, well-kept rooms
Unique decor and antiques, characterful in every corner
Attentive owner who helps arrange trips and recommends places
Fresh-cooked breakfast to order · shady garden with a fountain, quiet
cons: In the Ngao area, far from town, market and pier — a car is needed
Only 6 rooms, book ahead · restaurant closes around 7 pm

entries.name: THANSILA Resort
entries.revCount: 38 reviews · 5–8 min walk to the hot spring · renovated 2023
entries.badge: ♨️ Riverside, walk to the hot spring
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Raksawarin hot-spring area · Bang Rin · Ranong
tags: ♨️ 5–8 min walk to the Raksawarin hot spring
entries.addr: 129/2 Moo 1, Soi Thara, Bang Rin, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: THANSILA Resort is a small riverside resort in the Raksawarin hot-spring area, within a 5–8 minute walk of the hot spring, scoring 8.0. Renovated in 2023, it has around 19 rooms with both river-view and mountain-view options, all with a balcony. Real reviews praise the location near the hot spring, the lovely river views and the calm — waking up on the balcony looking out over the river and mountains feels relaxing — plus an easygoing owner, a pet-friendly policy and free bikes. Worth knowing: the breakfast is very simple, some rooms have firm beds and are small, the Wi-Fi isn't strong in every room, and it's about 3–4 km out of town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a river-view room for the best atmosphere — there are only a few, so book ahead. In the morning you can walk to soak at the Raksawarin hot spring. The breakfast is simple, so if you eat heartily, head to a restaurant near the hot spring.
pros: Near the Raksawarin hot spring, a 5–8 minute walk
Lovely river-view rooms, a quiet riverside feel
Renovated in 2023, cleaner than expected
Easygoing owner, pet-friendly · free bikes and parking
cons: Very simple breakfast · some rooms have firm beds and are small · Wi-Fi not strong everywhere
About 3–4 km out of town, a car is needed for the centre or pier

entries.name: Jansom Beach Resort Ranong
entries.revCount: 11 reviews · private beach at Pak Nam · Myanmar-side island views
entries.storyHtml: Jansom Beach Resort is a seafront resort at Pak Nam that sells mainly on a quiet private beach and rare views of the Myanmar-side islands, scoring 7.4. Real reviews praise the beautiful sea and sunset views, the quiet private beach, spacious rooms with wooden furniture and sea-facing private balconies, tasty, affordable resort-restaurant food, and friendly staff. Its strengths are the seafront location and the views. Worth knowing: the resort is ageing and looks worn in places, the pool isn't always well kept and gets cloudy at times, the beach needs washed-up debris cleared periodically, and it's out of town with a quiet, isolated approach, so a car is needed.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For full sea views, pick a Superior Sea View or the Deluxe Bungalow closest to the beach. The approach is quiet and isolated, so a car is safer and more convenient. It's near the pier, ideal if you're heading out by boat or for the sunset.
pros: Quiet private beach with beautiful sea and sunset views
Spacious rooms, wooden furniture, sea-facing private balconies
Tasty, affordable resort-restaurant food, Thai and Western breakfast
Rare Myanmar-side island views · friendly staff, free parking
cons: Ageing resort · pool not always well kept, cloudy at times
Beach needs debris cleared periodically · out of town, isolated approach, a car is needed

entries.name: B.C. Badin Resort
entries.revCount: 127 reviews · Thai-style houses on a hill · Myanmar-side sea views
entries.badge: 🌊 Hilltop sea views, near the pier
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pak Nam Ranong · near the Koh Phayam pier
tags: 🌊 Hilltop sea views over Myanmar-side islands
🏊 Pool + kids' pool, good for families
🏡 Thai-style houses in a shady garden
entries.storyHtml: B.C. Badin Resort is a seaside resort at Pak Nam, Thai-style houses on a hill with views over the sea and the Myanmar-side islands, scoring 7.4 from 127 reviews — among the most reviewed of the seafront group. Real reviews praise the lovely hilltop sea views, the quiet feel in a shady garden, a pool and kids' pool good for families, balconies to relax on all day, and a location near the Koh Phayam pier that suits anyone heading out by boat or crossing to the Myanmar side. Worth knowing: the resort and some rooms are ageing, the hot water is inconsistent and Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms, and it's away from the town centre and hot springs, so a car is needed.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For sea views, pick a Deluxe Sea View with a sea-facing balcony. Staff will let you see the room before choosing, so compare room condition at check-in. It's near the pier, handy as a base for Koh Phayam or the Myanmar-side crossing.
pros: Lovely hilltop sea views over the Myanmar-side islands
Quiet feel, Thai-style houses in a shady garden
An outdoor pool and kids' pool, good for families
Near the Koh Phayam pier · staff let you view rooms first · free parking
cons: Resort and some rooms are ageing · inconsistent hot water, weak Wi-Fi in some rooms
In the Pak Nam area, away from town and the hot springs, a car is needed

entries.name: Lamai Koh Phayam Resort
entries.revCount: 18 reviews · hillside bungalows, bay views · open year-round
entries.mrtTag: 📍 East-side hill · Koh Phayam · boat from Ranong
tags: 🏝️ Hillside bungalows with wide bay views
♨️ Hot water in the room, rare on the island
entries.storyHtml: Lamai Koh Phayam is a budget hillside resort on Koh Phayam selling wide bay views and a quiet feel, scoring 7.8 and open year-round. Real reviews praise the hilltop location with very wide bay and sea views, a scenic restaurant good for sitting morning and evening with a cool breeze all day, the quiet privacy, the light price, and hot water in the bathroom that's rare on the island. Its strengths are the views and the price. Worth knowing: the standard rooms are fan-only with no air-con, service and cleaning are inconsistent, the Wi-Fi is slow across the island, and it's on a hill with up-and-down walking, not ideal if walking is hard for you.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For air-con and a sea view, pick the Sea View Bungalow in the highest spot. Standard rooms are fan-only, so check the room type before booking. It's on a hill with up-and-down walking, so bring comfortable shoes.
pros: Hilltop location with very wide bay and sea views
Scenic restaurant, cool breeze all day, good morning and evening
Light price, private bungalows with balconies · a pool and massage room
Hot water in the bathroom, rare on the island
cons: Standard rooms are fan-only, no air-con · inconsistent service and cleaning
Island-wide slow Wi-Fi · on a hill with up-and-down walking

entries.name: Rattana's Resort
entries.revCount: 82 reviews · garden setting near the hot spring · Thai-Russian menu
entries.badge: 🌳 Garden setting, walk to the hot spring
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Thara · Bang Rin · Raksawarin hot-spring area
tags: ♨️ 5-min walk to the Raksawarin hot spring
🍽️ Good food, Thai and Russian menu
entries.addr: 127/35 Moo 1, Soi Thara, Bang Rin, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: Rattana's Resort is a garden resort in the Raksawarin hot-spring area within a 5-minute walk of the hot spring, at a light price, scoring 7.3 from 82 reviews. Real reviews praise the quiet garden setting, the easygoing and very helpful owner and staff, rooms more spacious than the price suggests with a balcony in nearly all of them, tasty food with both Thai and Russian menus, and a location near the bus station for onward travel to Koh Phayam. Its strengths are the garden feel and value. Worth knowing: the Wi-Fi is weak and unstable across the resort, room condition is inconsistent with some not well kept, the air-con is noisy in some rooms, and it's an older resort that needs more upkeep.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the full garden feel, ask for the mountain-view Studio or a room with a balcony. The Wi-Fi is weak, so bring a mobile data plan if you need to be online. In the morning you can easily walk to soak at the Raksawarin hot spring.
pros: Quiet garden setting, a 5-minute walk to the Raksawarin hot spring
Easygoing and very helpful owner and staff
Rooms more spacious than the price, balcony in nearly all of them
Good food, Thai and Russian menu · bike hire and free parking
cons: Weak, unstable Wi-Fi across the resort · inconsistent room condition
Noisy air-con in some rooms · an older resort that needs more upkeep

entries.name: Ranong Backpacker's Hostel
entries.revCount: 12 reviews · on the walking street · central
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Niwet · on the Ranong walking street · central
tags: 🚢 Near the pier for Koh Phayam
entries.addr: 240/9 Rueang Rat Rd, Khao Niwet, Mueang Ranong
entries.storyHtml: Ranong Backpacker's Hostel is a central backpacker hostel right by the walking street and the park, from ฿350 a bed, scoring 8.0. Real reviews praise the central location within walking distance of the walking street and restaurants, the budget price that suits backpackers, the easygoing and helpful owner and staff, bike hire, a shared kitchen and a 24h front desk, and a spot near the pier that makes it a handy base for Koh Phayam. Worth knowing: it's a small, older hostel with simple rooms, there's no breakfast, some nights carry street or roommate noise, and with very few rooms you should book ahead in high season.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more privacy, pick a Standard Double or Twin instead of a dorm. It's on the walking street, so some nights have noise — bring earplugs if you're sensitive. Hire a bike to get around town and to the pier.

Budget price from ฿350 a bed, suits backpackers
Easygoing and helpful owner and staff
Bike hire, shared kitchen, 24h front desk · near the Koh Phayam pier
cons: Small, older hostel with simple rooms · no breakfast
Some nights carry street or roommate noise · few rooms, book ahead in high season

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms and may change by date and season. faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Ranong hotels

faq.q: ❓ Where should travellers stay in Ranong?
faq.a: It depends on what you want to do · Ranong town suits walking the old quarter, food and onward transport (Tinidee, A Day Inn, Greenish, TOBEDzZ, Ranong Backpacker's) · The Raksawarin hot-spring area suits those coming to soak, within walking distance of the springs (THANSILA, Rattana's) · Pak Nam suits those after the seafront and Myanmar-side island views (Jansom Beach, B.C. Badin) · Koh Phayam suits those wanting to sleep right by the sea (The Blue Sky, Lamai Koh Phayam)

faq.q: ❓ How much do Ranong hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary: hostels and dorm beds start around ฿250–350/bed · town hotels and resorts around ฿650–1,100 · Pak Nam seafront resorts around ฿1,200–1,800 · boutiques from around ฿1,590 · and a Koh Phayam villa like The Blue Sky starts around ฿3,200 · Over high season and long weekends, prices can run higher than usual, so book ahead

faq.q: ❓ Which Ranong stays have hot mineral water?
faq.a: Tinidee Hotel@Ranong pipes natural hot mineral water into the bathroom so you can soak in a mineral bath in your own room, and has a mineral pool on site · And hot-spring-area stays like THANSILA Resort and Rattana's Resort are within a few minutes' walk of the public Raksawarin hot spring, where you can soak in the mineral water for free

faq.q: ❓ How do I get to Koh Phayam and where should I stay?
faq.a: Koh Phayam is a 45-minute to 2-hour boat ride from the Ranong pier, then motorbike on the island · The island stays open year-round in this guide are The Blue Sky Resort (mangrove villas) and Lamai Koh Phayam Resort (hillside bungalows) · Book your stay and check boat times ahead, especially in high season — many town stays will book ferry tickets for you

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car to explore Ranong?
faq.a: If you stay in town, you can walk the old quarter, markets and restaurants, so a car isn't essential · But the hot-spring-area, Pak Nam and seafront resorts are out of town, where having a car or being ready to hail a ride helps a lot · On Koh Phayam you mainly use a motorbike, which you can rent on the island

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Ranong hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so compare all 3 before booking every time — each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save hundreds of baht a night
